method: Same-agent bilingual close reading of the complete 24-block source and Marathi target, reverse paraphrase of the finite-model and infinite-time arguments, comparison with the preceding representation and verification units, and exact structural QA after seven bounded source-correction projections. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Trakhtenbrot's theorem: finite-model satisfiability is undecidable, and no effective sound-and-complete derivation system exists for validity over finite structures.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The preceding encoding reduces halting to validity and satisfiability over arbitrary structures. Finite-structure validity and finite-model satisfiability remain separate questions, so the proof is adapted to finite models.
samples.checks: The references to the two earlier verification lemmas and the validity and satisfiability theorem are intact. Finite versus infinite structures and the existential versus universal finite-model questions remain distinct.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If M halts after k steps, its actual run can be represented within a capped finite domain. The cap must exceed both the furthest possible head position and the last occupied input square, since the cap is reflexive under the chosen finite order. Conversely, old T(M,w) can have a spurious finite halting witness for a looping machine, so a stronger run theory is needed.
samples.checks: The corrected cap is max(k+1,len(w)+1), with OLTUR-017. The single-state stay-loop exercise preserves its domain, capped successor, order pairs and both required sentences; OLTUR-018 corrects only its undeclared state name and structure prime mark.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The strengthened T'(M,w) retains the number and initial-tape axioms, adds B(y') to each right, left and stay transition, and thereby makes the successor time distinct from all earlier numeral values. For a positive-position left move, A must exclude the old head square x' that gets overwritten.
samples.checks: All three transition directions, both left-boundary branches, the disequality formula B and the time-versus-position argument roles are preserved. OLTUR-019 corrects the first left branch's frame argument and its omitted B condition; the zero branch is unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For a halting run, the capped actual-run structure has a finite domain and satisfies both strengthened T' and the halting sentence !E. The source leaves the detailed satisfaction check as an exercise.
samples.checks: The successor and order interpretation, minimum halting step k and finite domain are preserved, with the corrected cap. OLTUR-020 aligns the final proof assertion and exercise with the lemma's exact T' and !E conjunction.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For a nonhalting machine, any model of T' and !E must have distinct values for arbitrarily many time numerals: a reached configuration at each positive time has B(n), and the numeral order makes each earlier k less than n. Such a model cannot be finite.
samples.checks: OLTUR-021 makes the assumed model satisfy T' rather than old T. OLTUR-022 restricts B(n) to times after at least one transition; no initial B(0) axiom exists, and positive times suffice for the infinite-domain argument. The source's omitted subproof remains an exercise.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A finite-satisfiability decider would decide whether M halts by testing the computable T'(M,w) and !E sentence, contradicting the halting theorem. The corollary rules out an effective proof system both sound and complete for validity in all finite structures; its proof remains an exercise using the complementary finite-model property and two one-sided procedures.
samples.checks: The two finite-model lemmas, reduction direction, undecidability claim and exercise reference remain intact. T351's explicit finite-model wording is kept separate from T199's every-finite-subset compactness sense.

source_observations: OLTUR-017: frozen cap max(k,len(w)) can omit the head's position k+1 and can put the last input square at the reflexive cap, making it spuriously blank. The Marathi uses max(k+1,len(w)+1).
OLTUR-018: frozen one-state exercise uses undeclared q and one M-prime assignment amid M-double-prime definitions; both are made consistent.
OLTUR-019: frozen positive left-move clause excludes the wrong tape square and omits B(y'); both are supplied while the zero branch remains unchanged.
OLTUR-020: frozen finite-model proof and exercise misstate the lemma's T' and !E conjunction; the Marathi checks the stated formula.
OLTUR-021: frozen converse proof starts with a model of T rather than the T' used in its following entailment; the Marathi assumes T'.
OLTUR-022: frozen fresh-time induction includes unaxiomatized B(0); the Marathi uses B(n) at positive times only.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The finite-model and infinite-time subproofs explicitly left as exercises in the frozen source are not supplied by this translation.
A coherent reader build and visual inspection are still pending.
